hypothesis: When a host pays a symbiont only for matching the host's m compressed measurements of a cooperative contribution, symbionts evolving under a per-unit (L1) production cost exploit the host with a gap (reward paid minus benefit delivered) that collapses abruptly at the basis-pursuit recovery transition m*, not smoothly in m.
mechanism: Coset-bounded sanctions. Any contribution x in the coset x_good + ker A is paid in full; under L1 cost the cheapest element of that coset equals x_good exactly when m is above the L1 recovery transition for the k-sparse x_good, and is a cheaper, less beneficial vector below it. Evolution under L1 cost should therefore discover coset aliases only below m*.
intervention: Symbiont population evolves under fitness = reward(A x) - c*||x||_1 at each host measurement count m in the grid.
control: Identical world with cost c*||x||_2^2 (the null twin); cost of the cooperator x_good is equal in both (10).
positive_control: For every (seed, m), the minimum-L1 element of x_good + ker A (linear program): the optimal L1 cheater, paid full reward by construction.
observable: g(seed, m) = population median of reward_i - benefit_i after the final generation (the exploitation gap). gbar(m) = mean of g over seeds. Reward = exp(-||A x - A x_good||^2 / (2 tau^2 ||A x_good||^2)); benefit = mean over required set R of clip(x_i, 0, 1).

success_clauses.text: The gap collapses at the recovery transition: sharpness = (gbar(m*-8) - gbar(m*+8)) / (gbar(m_min) - gbar(m_max)) is at least 0.6; defined as 0 if the total drop gbar(m_min) - gbar(m_max) is below 0.3.
No exploitation above the transition: mean of gbar(m) over m >= 40 is at most 0.05.

failure_clauses.text: No cheating evolved: total drop gbar(m_min) - gbar(m_max) below 0.3 (evolution did not find coset aliases at low m).
Exploitation persists above the transition: mean gbar over m >= 40 above 0.15.

alternative_explanation: Any shrinkage-inducing cost with a sparse cooperator gives the same collapse; the result would then be a property of L1 geometry (known compressed-sensing theory) acting through selection, and the symbiosis reading adds nothing beyond 'evolution approximately solves basis pursuit'.
null_twin: Same world, reward, verification matrices, selection, mutation and population, cost c*||x||_2^2 instead of c*||x||_1 (equal cost for x_good). The L2 coset optimum is the row-space projection of x_good, whose benefit rises smoothly with m: exploitation is present but has no transition.
substrate: population (mutation-selection over real-valued contribution vectors with a linear verification oracle)
why_this_implementation: The claim is about which vectors selection finds inside the host's measurement coset, so the organism is the contribution vector itself and the host is a matrix; the L1 vs L2 cost swap removes exactly the sparsity geometry while keeping every other quantity equal. Displaced alternatives: a principal-agent game solved analytically (would assume optimal cheaters, which is what is being tested) and learned agents (add credit assignment noise unrelated to the coset).
size: n=64, k=10, m in {12,16,...,60} (13 values), population 60, 2000 generations, truncation 50%, per-gene mutation prob 0.1 with N(0, 0.05^2), c=0.03, tau=0.25; treatment 10 seeds (0-9); controls 5 seeds (0-4) + 20 calibration draws per m
cost_estimate: treatment about 0.5 CPU core-minute (130 runs x ~0.2 s); controls about 0.5 core-minute
stupid_explanations: the reward tolerance tau sets a gap floor that is the same at all m, so the drop is carried by a few low-m points
the benefit clip at 1 creates a threshold unrelated to the coset geometry
A is scaled by 1/sqrt(m), so a mutation moves A x by a different relative amount at each m and selection strength varies with m, producing a step for reasons of search rather than geometry
2000 generations are enough to reach the coset optimum only when ker A is small (large m), so the gap falls wherever search becomes easy, not where L1 recovery sets in

parameters.m_star_rule: smallest grid m where basis pursuit recovers x_good exactly (max abs error < 1e-4) in >= 50% of calibration draws
